opening.spoken: This record covers the claimed solution of Navier–Stokes existence and smoothness: what has been claimed, what it rests on, and what would have to be checked by whom.

short_version.spoken: On 8 September 2026 OpenAI announced that an internal model had constructed, for every positive viscosity, a smooth force compactly supported in space and time and a solution of the three-dimensional Navier–Stokes equations starting from rest whose velocity becomes unbounded in finite time while its kinetic energy stays bounded, on space and on the torus. In the Clay formulation this is alternatives (C) and (D), which allow a force; alternatives (A) and (B), the unforced existence question, are untouched, and the day before the announcement Tristan Buckmaster had posted that he and Levent Alpöge had forced blow-up for the Euler equations by the same program, which they credit to Córdoba and Martínez-Zoroa. A Lean development accompanies the paper. A third party reports building it in October: no sorry, the three standard axioms, and statements identical to DeepMind's formal-conjectures file, which has since marked (C) and (D) as solved. A preprint by Bastounis, Circelli and Hansen reports that one lemma's Lean translation is weaker than the paper's statement, without claiming the result fails. No referee report exists. In November Alpöge and Buckmaster claimed the unforced case, recorded separately.

cycles.spoken: Tristan Buckmaster posted a statement that he and Levent Alpöge had forced blow-up for the incompressible porous media, Boussinesq and Euler equations, crediting the program to Córdoba and Martínez-Zoroa and alleging that OpenAI had learned of their progress. OpenAI announced the result on its blog and at a press briefing by Sébastien Bubeck; the paper's metadata dates it 19:06 UTC. OpenAI denied Buckmaster's allegation. Scientific American quoted Luis Silvestre and Diego Córdoba, the latter saying it would be a big surprise if done. The repository openai/NavierStokesAndEuler reached its second and current commit, under Apache-2.0, with Comparator challenge files that take their reference statements from DeepMind's formal-conjectures. Bastounis, Circelli and Hansen posted arXiv 2610.08144, reporting that the Lean estimate corresponding to the paper's Lemma 8.6 uses one more derivative than the paper's inequality, and similar mismatches elsewhere, while stating that they make no claim about the correctness of the written proof. A Zenodo record by Deep Bhattacharjee reports an independent build of the development at commit f9e8bc5 on Lean v4.34.0-rc2: 816 files with no sorry, native_decide or new axiom; both statements on exactly the three standard axioms; the sixteen definitions and both statements identical to formal-conjectures at commit 8bf45ed. Machine and wall time are not stated. DeepMind's formal-conjectures file for the problem, at its latest commit, lists alternatives (C) and (D) as solved, citing an internal OpenAI model, and (A) and (B) as open. Alpöge and Buckmaster posted a claimed unforced blow-up for Navier–Stokes, recorded as DEBRIEF-math-navierstokes. Nervous Machine fetched the paper (sha256 0e779481…, 2,959,204 bytes) and pinned the repository at its second commit. The Clay Mathematics Institute's problem page lists the problem as Active.

background.spoken: Do smooth solutions of the three-dimensional incompressible Navier–Stokes equations, started from smooth data, stay smooth for all time, or can the velocity become unbounded in finite time? Fefferman's formulation accepts either answer: a proof of existence and smoothness, with no force on space (A) or on the torus (B), or a proof of breakdown, which may use a smooth force, on space (C) or on the torus (D). This claim is (C) and (D) with a force. A third-party Lean formalization of all four alternatives exists in DeepMind's formal-conjectures, and the development's Comparator files take their reference statements from it.

background.spoken: The paper's main result says that for every positive viscosity there are a smooth force with compact support in space and time, a compact set, and smooth velocity and pressure fields on space, starting from zero velocity, supported in that set, with bounded kinetic energy, whose velocity becomes unbounded as time approaches one; and so no smooth solution with that force and datum exists for all time with bounded energy. Compact support carries the construction to the torus. The paper names these as alternatives (C) and (D) of Fefferman's formulation. A companion paper claims unforced blow-up for the Euler equations. The repository's metadata file records four main results with zero sorry and the three standard axioms, lists GPT-6 Astra in the Codex framework as the method, and records the review status as self-assessed. The press reported experts who regard the force as a loophole in the problem's wording and others who called the result a surprise if it holds. Buckmaster's statement of 7 September alleges that OpenAI adopted his and Alpöge's method after learning of their progress, which OpenAI denies; the statement says the pair's own forced results were checked in Lean on 22 August.
